subject: Medieval India

questions.q:
According to Portuguese writer Nuniz, the women in the Vijayanagara Empire were experts in which of the following areas?
1. Wrestling
2. Astrology
3. Accounting
4. Soothsaying
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.explain: Founded in 1336, Vijayanagara, literally 'city of victory', attracted a number of international travellers such as the Italian, Niccolo di Conti, the Portuguese Domingo Paes, Fernao Nuniz and Duarte Barbosa and the Afghan Abd, al-Razzaq, who have left vivid accounts of the city. Fernao Nuniz was a Portuguese traveller, chronicler and horse trader who spent three years in Vijayanagara. Nuniz writes: 'he (the king of Vijaynagar) has also women who wrestle, and others who are astrologers and soothsayers; and he has a woman who writes all the accounts of expenses that are incurred inside the gates and others whose duty it is to write all the affairs of the kingdom and compare their books with those of the writers outside; he has women also for music, who play instruments and sing. Even the wives of the king are well versed in music…it is said that he has judges, as well as bailiffs and watchmen who every night guard the palace, and these are women.'

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Saint Nimbarka was a contemporary of Akbar.
2. Saint Kabir was greatly influenced by Shaikh Ahmad Sirhindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is not correct: Saint Nimbarka was not a contemporary of Akbar because the history of Akbar dates down to the 16th century AD (1556 to 1605 AD). Akbar was the son of Humayun, who ruled over India for 26 years. The advent of the Mughal rule brought rich culture and ethical changes in India. Nimbarka, also called Nimbaditya or Niyamananda, was a Telugu-speaking Brahman who flourished in the 13th century in South India. He was a yogi, philosopher, and prominent astronomer.\n\nStatement 2 is not correct: Sant Kabir Das was a renowned saint, poet and social reformer of India who lived during the 15th century. His writings significantly influenced the Bhakti movement. Some of his famous writings include 'Sakhi Granth', 'Anurag Sagar', 'Bijak' and 'Kabir Granthawali'. He also founded a religious community named 'Kabir Panth' whose members are referred to as 'Kabir Panthis', implying the followers of Kabir Das. Vaishnava saint Swami Ramananda, who accepted Kabir as his disciple, greatly influenced his ideologies. Saint Kabir was 15th century poet whereas Sirhindi was in 17th century.

questions.q:
With reference to the cultural history of medieval India, consider the following statements:
1. Siddhas (sittars) of the Tamil region were monotheistic and condemned idolatry.
2. Lingayats of the Kannada region questioned the theory of rebirth and rejected the caste hierarchy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 1 is correct: Siddhas (Sittars) of the Tamil region were monotheistic (who are characterized by the belief that there is only one God) and they condemned idolatry, they advocated renunciation of the world.\n\nStatement 2 is correct: Lingayats are the followers of the 12th-century social reformer-philosopher poet, Basaveshwara. Basaveshwara was against the caste system and Vedic rituals. The term Lingayat denotes a person who wears a personal linga, an iconic form of the god Shiva, on the body which is received during the initiation ceremony. The Lingayats are strict monotheists. They enjoin the worship of only one God, namely, Linga (Shiva). They also questioned the theory of rebirth. They believed that on death, the devotee will be united with Shiva and will not return to this world.
